On Friday, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani celebrated Raksha Bandhan, a
traditionally Hindu festival that honors the bond between brothers and
sisters, by visiting India Home, a community center for South Asian seniors.
The next day in New York, a leader of a far-right, [Nazi-
inspired](https://caravanmagazine.in/history/rss-golwalkar-links-nazism) Hindu
nationalist [paramilitary organization](https://www.dw.com/en/india-at-a-
crossroads-100-years-of-thehindu-nationalist-rss-movement/video-74253317)
delivered remarks at Madison Square Garden.

Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat spoke Saturday at a
rally in New York City, called the "Universal Oneness Celebration," an event
ostensibly about shared humanity and mutual respect. "If any Hindu thinks that
there should be no Muslim in Bharat, he will not remain Hindu," a moderate-
sounding Bhagwat [said](https://x.com/sidhant/status/2093765068156813401?s=20)
("Bharat" is another name for India). "If you call yourself Hindu, you must
believe all paths are leading to the same goal."

However, in the past, Bhagwat has attracted controversy by
[declaring](https://www.thequint.com/news/india/rss-chief-mohan-bhagwat-army-
women-controversial-statements#read-more) "everyone born in" India to be a
Hindu, "even Muslims"; [suggesting](https://www.thequint.com/news/india/rss-
chief-mohan-bhagwat-army-women-controversial-statements#read-more) gang rape
in India is a Western import; and
[accusing](https://caravanmagazine.in/vantage/why-mohan-bhagwats-recent-
statements-are-testament-rsss-core-ideology) Muslim men of carrying out "love
jihad" by courting Hindu women.

Hence, the RSS rally at Madison Square Garden on Saturday attracted large
[protests](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/hundreds-protest-hindu-
nationalist-paramilitary-leader-mohan-bhagwat-visit-new-york-city) outside.
While several organizations tried and failed to stop the rally from taking
place, in protest of Bhagwat's controversial political movement, the
opposition continues.

Nearly 100 political officials across the United States - from Michigan Senate
candidate Abdul El-Sayed and his former opponent Haley Stevens, to top Indian-
American Reps. Ro Khanna and Pramila Jayapal - have now pledged to reject
money from the RSS.
